regulator: Energy Safe Victoria; Victorian Building Authority (Building and Plumbing Commission); WorkSafe Victoria / Asbestos Victoria
notes: Verified Victorian DIY policy. Each definite rule cites an official Victorian regulator. Rules are task-specific; no broad allowances. Where official guidance is ambiguous the rule is 'unclear', never 'permitted'. See docs/diy-policy/victoria-sources.md for the source review.

rules.source_regulator: Energy Safe Victoria
rules.reason: In Victoria all electrical installation work — including small jobs such as replacing power points and light switches — must be done by a licensed electrician. Unlicensed electrical work is illegal and dangerous.
warning_signs: Live electrical work can cause electrocution and fire
prohibited_actions: Do not carry out or attempt this electrical work yourself

rules.source_regulator: Energy Safe Victoria
rules.reason: Exposed or damaged wiring is electrical installation work and a live hazard. It must be isolated and repaired by a licensed electrician; do not touch it.
warning_signs: Exposed wiring may be live and can be lethal — do not touch and keep clear
prohibited_actions: Do not touch, tape over, or attempt to repair exposed wiring yourself

rules.source_regulator: Energy Safe Victoria
rules.reason: Gas fitting and gas-appliance connection/disconnection in Victoria must always be done by a licensed gasfitter. Unlicensed gas work is illegal and can be fatal.
warning_signs: Gas work carries fire, explosion and carbon monoxide risks
prohibited_actions: Do not connect, disconnect, or work on gas lines or gas appliances yourself

rules.source_regulator: Victorian Building Authority (Building and Plumbing Commission)
rules.reason: This is regulated plumbing work under the Plumbing Regulations 2018 and must be carried out by a licensed or registered plumber. Work valued over $750 also requires a plumbing compliance certificate.
prohibited_actions: Do not carry out water-supply plumbing work yourself

rules.required_professional_type: Licensed plumber endorsed in backflow prevention
rules.source_regulator: Victorian Building Authority (Building and Plumbing Commission)
rules.reason: Backflow prevention work must be done by a licensed plumber holding the backflow prevention endorsement; testing must be recorded and lodged.
prohibited_actions: Do not install, test, or work on backflow prevention devices yourself

rules.source_regulator: Victorian Building Authority (Building and Plumbing Commission)
rules.reason: Most plumbing work in Victoria must be done by a licensed plumber. Whether a specific minor maintenance task (for example replacing a tap washer) is exempt is not clearly defined, so this is treated as unclear — confirm with the VBA before proceeding.
questions_required: Exactly what is the task (e.g. replace a tap washer, or replace/move a fixture)?
Does the work involve any pipe, drain, or fixture connection or disconnection?

rules.required_professional_type: Registered building practitioner (building permit and registered building surveyor required)
rules.source_regulator: Victorian Building Authority (Building and Plumbing Commission)
rules.reason: Structural building work (including altering or removing load-bearing elements) requires a building permit and must be carried out by a registered building practitioner; a registered building surveyor issues the permit.
prohibited_actions: Do not alter or remove load-bearing or structural elements without a permit

rules.required_professional_type: Registered building practitioner (building permit and registered building surveyor required)
rules.source_regulator: Victorian Building Authority (Building and Plumbing Commission)
rules.reason: Cracking that indicates structural movement is structural building work. It must be assessed by a registered building practitioner (and may need a structural engineer); repairs may require a building permit.
warning_signs: Wide, diagonal, recurring cracks or sticking doors/windows can indicate footing or structural movement
questions_required: Is the crack wider than 3mm, diagonal, or growing over time?
Are doors or windows sticking, or is there any floor movement?

rules.source_regulator: WorkSafe Victoria / Asbestos Victoria
rules.reason: Material suspected to contain asbestos must be identified before any work. Asbestos removal is best performed by a WorkSafe-licensed removalist; friable asbestos and larger non-friable quantities must be. Because the material is only suspected, this is treated as unclear pending identification.
warning_signs: Disturbing asbestos can release lethal fibres — do not cut, drill, sand or break it
questions_required: Has the material been tested and confirmed as asbestos?
Was the building built or last renovated before 1990?

conditions: Cosmetic repainting of existing, sound surfaces only
exclusions: Does not cover any electrical, plumbing, gas or structural work
Does not cover disturbing surfaces that may contain asbestos or lead paint
rules.source_regulator: Victorian Building Authority (Building and Plumbing Commission)
rules.reason: Repainting existing surfaces is maintenance that does not require a building permit and is not a licensed trade in Victoria.
allowed_actions: Repaint existing walls, ceilings, trim and doors

conditions: Non-structural cosmetic patching of small cracks or holes only
exclusions: Excludes cracks indicating structural movement (wide, diagonal, recurring, or with sticking doors/windows)
Excludes any sheet/wall that may contain asbestos (pre-1990 construction)
rules.source_regulator: Victorian Building Authority (Building and Plumbing Commission)
rules.reason: Minor, non-structural plaster patching (small cracks or holes) is maintenance and does not require a building permit or licence. If the cracking may be structural it must instead be assessed by a building practitioner.
warning_signs: A wide, diagonal or recurring crack may indicate structural movement — treat as structural work, not cosmetic
allowed_actions: Fill and sand small non-structural cracks and holes, then repaint

rules.source_regulator: WorkSafe Victoria / Asbestos Victoria
rules.reason: The surface material and work type could not be identified. More information is required before any DIY assessment; in older buildings, unidentified sheet material may contain asbestos.
questions_required: How old is the building — could the material contain asbestos (pre-1990)?
What exactly needs to be done?

rules.source_regulator: WorkSafe Victoria / Asbestos Victoria
rules.reason: Working at height is a safety risk rather than a licensing question for a homeowner. WorkSafe Victoria duties apply where others are engaged. Use proper fall-prevention and consider engaging a professional for roof-level work.
warning_signs: Falls from height are a leading cause of serious injury
